label: first input token is h (t=0)
explanation: Fires at a near-constant ~1.89 at step 0 when the first original token is h; never fires on any other token, in the delimiter or copy phase, or at t>=2. The only other activations are a weak echo (~0.07, about 4% of max, 0.1% of mass) at t=1 when the sequence starts with h h. Magnitude does not depend on L or the rest of the sequence.

issues: Every factual claim checks out. On test: precision 1.0, recall 0.967, F1 0.983, mass recall 0.999, correlation 0.99997. On dev: fires only on in_tok h, only in the original phase, only at t=0 (0.999 of mass) and t=1 (0.001 of mass). No activations in the delimiter or copy phase, none at t>=2. Max is 1.888 and the median is 1.888.

The misses are not random: all 569 test misses are the disclosed echo at t=1 in sequences that start with 'h h', at about 0.04 of max. The explanation already states this, and it carries only 0.1% of activation mass, so the label is not overclaiming.
There are 0 false positives on test.
Minor: the label leaves out the 'h h' echo. Adding it gives a perfect predicate on test (F1 1.0), though correlation drops slightly to 0.984 because it treats the weak echo as full activation.
